## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 93de21ca4af4279d8ac132e05a7692a7b75730f5

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** The fix commit (`80dcd036`) replaces four call sites that use `Biweekly.write(ical).go(...)` with explicit `ICalWriter` instances that set `writer.getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(TimeZone.getDefault())` before writing. I used `git log -S "Biweekly.write(ical)"` on each of the four touched files (`EventEmail.java`, `EventsExportEventsToICal.java`, `CalendarServlet.java`, `CalendarExport.java`) to find every commit that added or removed that exact call pattern. In all four files, the only two commits matching were `93de21ca` (added it) and `80dcd036` (removed/replaced it) — no other commit ever touched this code path in between.

**(2) Specific change:** `93de21ca` ("migrate to the biweekly iCal library") replaced UniTime's hand-rolled, line-by-line `.ics` text generation (which explicitly wrote `X-WR-TIMEZONE:` and other fields using `TimeZone.getDefault()`) with calls to the Biweekly library's convenience method `Biweekly.write(ical).go()`. That convenience writer has no knowledge of which timezone `DateStart`/`DateEnd` properties should be serialized in — without an explicit `TimezoneInfo` configured on the writer, Biweekly falls back to writing date-times as UTC/floating rather than using the server's local default timezone. This silently produced incorrect meeting times in exported/emailed calendars whenever the server's default timezone wasn't UTC.

**(3) Evidence:** 
- `git show 93de21ca` confirms this commit introduced `Biweekly.write(ical)...` in all four files that are touched by the fix, replacing manual `out.println(...)` iCal generation that had previously encoded the local timezone explicitly (e.g. `out.println("X-WR-TIMEZONE:"+TimeZone.getDefault().getID());`).
- No intervening commit modified these call sites — the `-S` search shows a clean two-commit history (`93de21ca` → `80dcd036`) for the exact `Biweekly.write(ical)` string in every affected file.
- The fix's core change is adding `writer.getTimezoneInfo().setDefaultTimeZone(TimeZone.getDefault())`, which is precisely the timezone-awareness that was lost when switching from the old manual serialization to `Biweekly.write(...)` in `93de21ca`.

I'm confident in this attribution given the precise, consistent match across all four files and the absence of any intermediate modifying commits, though I did not execute/test the Biweekly library behavior directly (read-only investigation) to observe the UTC-vs-local timezone output difference firsthand.
